components.note: 一 (one) — a single horizontal stroke is the number one; 二 and 三 just add strokes, so the first three numbers are tally marks.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 室 room, 安 safe, 字 character; 家 is home.
豕 (pig) — a pig under a roof: pigs were kept in the home, hence home and family.

example.hanzi: 周末我们一家去公园玩。
example.pinyin: zhōumò wǒmen yī jiā qù gōngyuán wán.
example.english: This weekend our whole family went to the park.
example.fact: The Rothschild banking family expanded across five European capitals in the early 1800s by sending each of five brothers to run a branch in a different city, coordinating investments and information faster than most governments of the era. Their family network is often cited as one of history's earliest examples of a coordinated multinational financial institution.

examples.hanzi: 我们一家都喜欢旅行。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yì jiā dōu xǐhuan lǚxíng.
examples.english: Our whole family loves traveling.

examples.hanzi: 他们是一家人，当然会互相帮助。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen shì yì jiārén, dāngrán huì hùxiāng bāngzhù.
examples.english: They're one family, so of course they help each other.

components.note: 囗 (enclosure) — boundaries: 国, 园, 图; 围 is to surround.
韦 (wéi) sounds exactly like 围; also in 违 wéi and 伟 wěi.

example.hanzi: 大家围着桌子坐下。
example.pinyin: Dàjiā wéi zhe zhuōzi zuòxià.
example.english: Everyone sat around the table.
example.fact: 围 is the verb 'to surround', with 围着 (around) for position. It also gives 周围 (surroundings), 围巾 (scarf) and 围棋, the board game Go, named for the idea of surrounding territory.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们围着老师问问题。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen wéi zhe lǎoshī wèn wèntí.
examples.english: The kids gathered around the teacher to ask questions.

examples.hanzi: 他在脖子上围了一条围巾。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài bózi shang wéi le yì tiáo wéijīn.
examples.english: He wrapped a scarf around his neck.

components.note: 广 (house) — the top-left cover, as in 店 shop and 床 bed; it marks a building or room.
隶 (servant) — inside 广. Dictionary story: a home with a servant, healthy and untroubled, hence 健康 health; origin is uncertain, so memory aid only.
复 (fù) sounds out 腹 fù belly and 覆 fù cover; as a word it means again or to repeat, as in 恢复, 重复.

example.hanzi: 经过治疗,他很快就康复了。
example.pinyin: jīngguò zhìliáo, tā hěn kuài jiù kāngfù le.
example.english: After treatment, he recovered quickly.
example.fact: Alexander Fleming's accidental discovery of penicillin in 1928, after noticing mold had killed bacteria in a contaminated petri dish, led to the first antibiotic that let doctors reliably help patients recover from infections that had previously often been fatal. Mass production of penicillin during World War II is estimated to have saved hundreds of thousands of soldiers' lives.

examples.hanzi: 奶奶住院一个月后康复了。
examples.pinyin: Nǎinai zhùyuàn yí ge yuè hòu kāngfù le.
examples.english: Grandma recovered after a month in the hospital.

examples.hanzi: 祝你早日康复！
examples.pinyin: Zhù nǐ zǎorì kāngfù!
examples.english: I wish you a speedy recovery!

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — marks bamboo and things made of it, as in 笔, 筷, 签; 策 was a bamboo whip or slip, then a plan.
朿 (cì) hints at the sound: 策 cè is close.
刂 (knife) — cutting, as in 到, 分, 别: 划 is to cut a line, then to plan (计划) or row (huá).

example.hanzi: 这次活动是由她策划的。
example.pinyin: zhè cì huódòng shì yóu tā cèhuà de.
example.english: This event was planned by her.
example.fact: The D-Day invasion of Normandy in 1944, codenamed Operation Overlord, was planned for more than a year by Allied commanders who coordinated deception campaigns, tidal charts, and weather forecasts down to a single viable launch window. Poor weather forced a one-day delay, and the operation still remains one of the largest and most meticulously planned amphibious assaults in military history.

examples.hanzi: 他们正在策划一次旅行。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen zhèngzài cèhuà yí cì lǚxíng.
examples.english: They are planning a trip.

examples.hanzi: 是谁策划了这场惊喜派对？
examples.pinyin: Shéi cèhuà le zhè chǎng jīngxǐ pàiduì?
examples.english: Who planned this surprise party?

components.note: 火 (fire) — a picture of flames, and a component seen in 烧, 灯, 热 (as the dots 灬), 炒; fire radical for burning and heat.
宀 (roof) — a roof over fire 火 means disaster; 宀 appears in 家 home, 安 safe.

example.hanzi: 消防员及时赶到,扑灭了火灾。
example.pinyin: xiāofángyuán jíshí gǎndào, pūmiè le huǒzāi.
example.english: Firefighters arrived in time and put out the fire.
example.fact: The Great Fire of London in 1666 burned for four days, destroying roughly 13,200 houses and 87 churches, including the original St. Paul's Cathedral, yet official records list only a handful of confirmed deaths. The disaster led directly to England's first building regulations requiring brick and stone construction instead of the wood and thatch that had let flames spread so fast.

examples.hanzi: 昨晚附近发生了一起火灾。
examples.pinyin: Zuówǎn fùjìn fāshēng le yì qǐ huǒzāi.
examples.english: A fire broke out nearby last night.

examples.hanzi: 这场火灾损失很大。
examples.pinyin: Zhè chǎng huǒzāi sǔnshī hěn dà.
examples.english: This fire caused heavy losses.

components.note: 贝 (cowry shell, money) — money and trade: 财, 货, 买, 贵; 费 is a cost or fee.
弗 (fú) is close to fèi; same part in 沸 fèi.
用 (use) — early picture is debated: a pail, a fenced enclosure or a hung bell. Memory aid: a door-frame 冂 with a cross-bar — a tool 'put to use' (使用, 不用).

example.hanzi: 这次旅行的费用超出了预算。
example.pinyin: zhè cì lǚxíng de fèiyòng chāochū le yùsuàn.
example.english: The cost of this trip exceeded the budget.
example.fact: NASA's Apollo program, which put twelve astronauts on the Moon between 1969 and 1972, cost roughly $25 billion at the time — equivalent to well over $150 billion in today's dollars. At its peak, the program consumed more than 4 percent of the entire U.S. federal budget.

examples.hanzi: 请问这里的学费和其他费用是多少？
examples.pinyin: Qǐngwèn zhèlǐ de xuéfèi hé qítā fèiyòng shì duōshao?
examples.english: Excuse me, how much are the tuition and other fees here?

examples.hanzi: 这笔费用由公司来付。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bǐ fèiyòng yóu gōngsī lái fù.
examples.english: The company will pay for this cost.

meanings: to make up for a deficiency

components.note: 弓 (bow) — marks bows and stretching, as in 张, 引, 弯; 弥 is to fill or extend.
尔 (ěr) is only a loose hint for mí.
衤 (clothing) — marks cloth, as in 衬, 衫, 裤; 补 is to mend a garment.
卜 (bǔ) gives the sound exactly: 补 bǔ.

example.hanzi: 他努力工作来弥补之前的错误。
example.pinyin: tā nǔlì gōngzuò lái míbǔ zhīqián de cuòwù.
example.english: He worked hard to make up for his earlier mistake.
example.fact: In the Japanese art of kintsugi, broken pottery is repaired using a lacquer mixed with powdered gold, deliberately highlighting the cracks rather than hiding them. The philosophy behind the practice treats a mended object as more beautiful for having been broken and repaired, rather than diminished by the damage.

examples.hanzi: 我想弥补对孩子的亏欠。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng míbǔ duì háizi de kuīqiàn.
examples.english: I want to make up for what I owe my child.

examples.hanzi: 他想用道歉来弥补过错。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng yòng dàoqiàn lái míbǔ guòcuò.
examples.english: He wants to make up for his mistake with an apology.

components.note: 大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.
门 (gate) — a picture of a two-leaf door; as a radical it frames characters of doors and openings — 开, 关, 问, 间.

example.hanzi: 学校的大门早上七点开。
example.pinyin: xuéxiào de dàmén zǎoshang qī diǎn kāi.
example.english: The school's main gate opens at 7am.
example.fact: Berlin's Brandenburg Gate was completed in 1791 as a grand city entrance but later became a stark symbol of division during the Cold War, standing just inside East Berlin with the Berlin Wall running directly behind it. When the wall fell in 1989, the gate became the central gathering point for celebrations of German reunification.

examples.hanzi: 请把大门关好。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ dàmén guān hǎo.
examples.english: Please close the front gate properly.

examples.hanzi: 我们在大门口等你。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zài dàménkǒu děng nǐ.
examples.english: We'll wait for you at the main entrance.

components.note: 辶 (movement) — marks walking and roads, as in 过, 进, 送; 连 is vehicles 车 moving in a line, joined together.
车 (cart) — the vehicle in the chain, as in 转, 轮; 链 liàn (chain) is built on 连.
扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: receiving something by hand.
妾 (qiè) is only a loose sound clue for jiē.

example.hanzi: 这座桥连接了两座城市。
example.pinyin: zhè zuò qiáo liánjiē le liǎng zuò chéngshì.
example.english: This bridge connects the two cities.
example.fact: The first successful transatlantic telegraph cable, completed in 1866 after an earlier attempt failed within weeks, connected Europe and North America directly for the first time, cutting message delivery from roughly ten days by ship to just minutes. The cable was over 4,300 kilometers long and laid across the ocean floor by a single ship, the SS Great Eastern.

examples.hanzi: 这根线连接着电视和电脑。
examples.pinyin: Zhè gēn xiàn liánjiē zhe diànshì hé diànnǎo.
examples.english: This cable connects the TV and the computer.

examples.hanzi: 手机已经连接到无线网络了。
examples.pinyin: Shǒujī yǐjīng liánjiē dào wúxiàn wǎngluò le.
examples.english: The phone has connected to the Wi-Fi.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh) — body-part radical, as in 肝 liver, 肺 lung, 脑 brain.
田 here is not a field but an old picture of a stomach holding food.

example.hanzi: 我的胃有点疼。
example.pinyin: Wǒ de wèi yǒudiǎn téng.
example.english: My stomach hurts a little.
example.fact: 胃 is the organ itself, whereas the belly is 肚子, so Chinese has two words where English has one 'stomach'. 胃口 ('stomach mouth') means 'appetite', and also 'taste' or 'liking' in a figurative sense.

examples.hanzi: 吃太多辣的东西对胃不好。
examples.pinyin: Chī tài duō là de dōngxi duì wèi bù hǎo.
examples.english: Eating too much spicy food is bad for your stomach.

examples.hanzi: 我没有胃口,不想吃饭。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ méiyǒu wèikǒu, bù xiǎng chīfàn.
examples.english: I have no appetite and don't want to eat.

components.note: 韦 (leather; from 韋) — the right half. 韩 is mainly a name today (Korea, surname Han); the parts no longer explain the meaning.
龺 (sunrays over a pole) — the left part, the same as in 乾 and 朝. Memory aid: just a visual block; say 'hán' by its look, not by its parts.
囗 (enclosure) — borders and walls, as in 园 garden, 圆 round, 回 return; 囗 is the country's boundary.
玉 (jade) — treasure within the border; the traditional 國 had 或 (defended territory) inside.

example.hanzi: 我打算下个月去韩国旅游。
example.pinyin: wǒ dǎsuàn xià gè yuè qù Hánguó lǚyóu.
example.english: I plan to travel to South Korea next month.
example.fact: South Korea's economy grew so quickly in the decades after the devastating 1950-53 Korean War that economists began calling it the 'Miracle on the Han River' — a nation with almost no industrial base transformed into one of the world's largest economies within a single generation. Its GDP per capita rose from among the lowest in the world in the 1960s to rival many wealthy Western nations today.

examples.hanzi: 我同事是韩国人。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ tóngshì shì Hánguó rén.
examples.english: My colleague is Korean.

examples.hanzi: 韩国的泡菜很有名。
examples.pinyin: Hánguó de pàocài hěn yǒumíng.
examples.english: Korean kimchi is very famous.

components.note: 王 (jade) — jade and gems, as in 球 ball, 玩 play, 现 appear: 理 first meant polishing jade along its grain, then reason.
里 (lǐ) gives the exact sound; also in 鲤 lǐ.
心 (heart) — thought and feelings, as in 思, 感, 急: to think of someone.
相 (xiāng) is a close sound clue for xiǎng; 相 also in 箱 xiāng and 湘 xiāng.

example.hanzi: 成为宇航员是他从小的理想。
example.pinyin: Chéngwéi yǔhángyuán shì tā cóngxiǎo de lǐxiǎng.
example.english: Becoming an astronaut was his ideal since childhood.
example.fact: Yuri Gagarin became the first human to reach space in April 1961, orbiting Earth once in the Vostok 1 capsule in about 108 minutes. He experienced weightlessness for nearly the entire flight, an experience so novel that engineers weren't sure a human could function afterward. His safe return proved otherwise and kicked off the space race in earnest.

examples.hanzi: 我的理想是当一名老师。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de lǐxiǎng shì dāng yì míng lǎoshī.
examples.english: My ideal is to become a teacher.

examples.hanzi: 这个计划听起来很理想。
examples.pinyin: Zhège jìhuà tīng qǐlai hěn lǐxiǎng.
examples.english: This plan sounds ideal.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement, as in 这, 近, 送: 过 is to pass or cross.
寸 here replaces 咼 (guō) of the traditional 過, so it is not a sound clue; 咼 survives in 锅 guō and 祸 huò.
攵 (tap, strike) — marks action and effort, as in 数, 教, 放, 改; 敏 is quick and sharp.
每 (měi) hints at the sound: 敏 mǐn is close.

example.hanzi: 我对花生过敏，吃了会全身起疹子。
example.pinyin: Wǒ duì huāshēng guòmǐn, chī le huì quánshēn qǐ zhěnzi.
example.english: I'm allergic to peanuts; eating them makes my whole body break out in hives.
example.fact: A peanut allergy occurs when the immune system mistakenly identifies harmless peanut proteins as a threat and releases histamine in response. Anaphylaxis, the most severe reaction, can constrict airways within minutes, which is why epinephrine auto-injectors work by rapidly relaxing smooth muscle and tightening blood vessels. Peanut allergies affect roughly 1-2% of children in the United States, and unlike some other food allergies, most children do not outgrow it.

examples.hanzi: 我对牛奶过敏，不能喝。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ duì niúnǎi guòmǐn, bù néng hē.
examples.english: I'm allergic to milk and can't drink it.

examples.hanzi: 春天一到，他就容易过敏。
examples.pinyin: Chūntiān yí dào, tā jiù róngyì guòmǐn.
examples.english: As soon as spring comes, he gets allergies easily.

components.note: 尚 (shàng) gives the rhyme; 党 is a simplification of 黨, which was 尚 over 黑.

example.hanzi: 他加入了一个新的政党。
example.pinyin: Tā jiārù le yí gè xīn de zhèngdǎng.
example.english: He joined a new political party.
example.fact: 党 is the word for a political party (政党, 党员 party member), and most often hints at the Communist Party in mainland context. Casually, -党 is a suffix for fans or camps, such as 甜党 / 咸党 in the sweet-or-salty tofu pudding debate.

examples.hanzi: 这个党的党员有很多。
examples.pinyin: Zhège dǎng de dǎngyuán yǒu hěn duō.
examples.english: This party has many members.

examples.hanzi: 选举中,那个党赢了。
examples.pinyin: Xuǎnjǔ zhōng, nàge dǎng yíng le.
examples.english: That party won the election.

components.note: 凯 (kǎi) — triumph, mostly seen in names; as a part it sounds out 铠 kǎi and 恺 kǎi.
牛 (ox) — cattle and animals, as in 物 thing, 牧 herd, 牺 sacrifice: 特 first meant a bull, then special.
寺 (sì) is only a loose sound clue for tè; 寺 also in 诗 shī and 持 chí.

example.hanzi: 凯特是我们班唯一的美国交换生。
example.pinyin: Kǎitè shì wǒmen bān wéiyī de Měiguó jiāohuànshēng.
example.english: Kate is the only American exchange student in our class.
example.fact: The name Kate is a short form of Catherine, which traces back to the Greek 'Aikaterine,' possibly linked to the goddess Hecate or to the Greek word 'katharos,' meaning pure. Catherine of Alexandria, a 4th-century martyr associated with a spiked wheel, gave rise to the term 'Catherine wheel' for both a torture device and, later, a spinning firework.

examples.hanzi: 凯特每天坐地铁上班。
examples.pinyin: Kǎitè měitiān zuò dìtiě shàngbān.
examples.english: Kate takes the subway to work every day.

examples.hanzi: 凯特请我们周末去她家吃饭。
examples.pinyin: Kǎitè qǐng wǒmen zhōumò qù tā jiā chīfàn.
examples.english: Kate invited us to her house for dinner this weekend.

components.note: 灬 (fire) — heat and burning, as in 热 hot, 照 shine, 黑 black; a dot is a small spot like a spark.
占 (zhàn) is a loose sound clue for diǎn; 占 also sounds out 站 zhàn and 粘 zhān.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 雨水打在窗户上，留下一个个小点子。
example.pinyin: Yǔshuǐ dǎ zài chuānghu shàng, liú xià yí gè gè xiǎo diǎnzi.
example.english: Raindrops hit the window, leaving little droplets behind.
example.fact: Contrary to the classic teardrop cartoon, falling raindrops are actually closer to the shape of a hamburger bun — rounded on top and flattened on the bottom — because air resistance pushes up against the drop as it falls. Drops larger than about 4 millimeters across become unstable and break apart into smaller droplets, which is why the biggest raindrops you'll ever see are roughly the size of a housefly.

examples.hanzi: 他脑子里总是有很多好点子。
examples.pinyin: Tā nǎozi lǐ zǒngshì yǒu hěn duō hǎo diǎnzi.
examples.english: He always has lots of good ideas in his head.

examples.hanzi: 你有什么点子吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yǒu shénme diǎnzi ma?
examples.english: Do you have any ideas?

components.note: 禾 (grain) — 禾 is grain, as in 种, 秋; 科 first meant grading grain with a measure 斗, and then categories like 科学.
斗 (dipper) — 斗 is a measuring dipper, as in 斗 (a unit of grain).
扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; 技 is hand skill.
支 (zhī) is a loose sound clue; same part in 枝 zhī and 肢 zhī.

example.hanzi: 这家公司专注于人工智能科技的研发。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī zhuānzhù yú réngōng zhìnéng kējì de yánfā.
example.english: This company focuses on researching and developing artificial intelligence technology.
example.fact: The term 'artificial intelligence' was coined in 1956 at a summer workshop at Dartmouth College, where researchers optimistically predicted machines could achieve human-level reasoning within a generation. Progress stalled for decades in periods researchers call 'AI winters,' when funding dried up after early promises went unmet. It took the rise of cheap parallel computing — largely from graphics cards originally built for video games — to make today's large-scale neural networks practical.

examples.hanzi: 科技改变了我们的生活。
examples.pinyin: Kējì gǎibiàn le wǒmen de shēnghuó.
examples.english: Technology has changed our lives.

examples.hanzi: 这家科技公司在上海。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā kējì gōngsī zài Shànghǎi.
examples.english: This tech company is in Shanghai.

components.note: 勹 (wrap) — a person curled around something; in 包 it wraps around a baby 巳, the original picture. 包 sounds out 抱 bào, 跑 pǎo, 泡 pào, 饱 bǎo.
衣 (clothing) — marks clothes and wrapping, as in 衬, 装, 袋; in 裹 the 衣 literally wraps around 果.
果 (guǒ) gives the sound exactly: 裹 guǒ.

example.hanzi: 邮递员今天送来了一个很重的包裹。
example.pinyin: Yóudìyuán jīntiān sòng lái le yí gè hěn zhòng de bāoguǒ.
example.english: The postal worker delivered a very heavy parcel today.
example.fact: The Universal Postal Union, founded in 1874, set common rules so a letter or parcel could cross national borders without needing separate postage for each country it passed through. Before that, international mail often required paying multiple, unpredictable fees along the route. Today the UPU coordinates postal service among 192 member countries, one of the oldest international organizations still in operation.

examples.hanzi: 请把这个包裹寄到北京。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ zhège bāoguǒ jì dào Běijīng.
examples.english: Please send this parcel to Beijing.

examples.hanzi: 我在门口收到了一个包裹。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài ménkǒu shōudào le yí ge bāoguǒ.
examples.english: I received a package at the door.

components.note: 工 (work) — a carpenter's tool shape: work, craftsman. 工 is a sound series: 红 hóng, 江 jiāng, 功 gōng, 空 kōng.
贝 (cowry shell, money) — wealth and trade: 财, 费, 买; 资 is capital or resources.
次 (cì) is a loose clue; same part in 姿 zī and 咨 zī.

example.hanzi: 公司这个月推迟了发工资的时间。
example.pinyin: Gōngsī zhège yuè tuīchí le fā gōngzī de shíjiān.
example.english: The company delayed the payday this month.
example.fact: The word 'salary' comes from the Latin 'salarium,' often linked to an allowance Roman soldiers reportedly received to buy salt, a valuable commodity used for preserving food before refrigeration existed. Whether soldiers were literally paid in salt is debated by historians, but salt was valuable enough in the ancient world to be traded along dedicated routes such as the Via Salaria, the 'salt road' leading to Rome.

examples.hanzi: 他的工资不高，但很稳定。
examples.pinyin: Tā de gōngzī bù gāo, dàn hěn wěndìng.
examples.english: His salary isn't high, but it's stable.

examples.hanzi: 这个月我的工资涨了一点。
examples.pinyin: Zhège yuè wǒ de gōngzī zhǎng le yìdiǎn.
examples.english: My pay went up a little this month.

components.note: 小 (small) — three small dots, tiny grains. As a radical it appears in 少 few, 尖 sharp.
小 (small) — three small dots, tiny grains. As a radical it appears in 少 few, 尖 sharp.
白 (white, bright) — 的 first meant bright and clear, as in 的确 dí què.
勺 (sháo) is a loose sound clue for dì; 勺 also sounds out 约 yuē and 钓 diào.

example.hanzi: 桌子上放着一个小小的花瓶。
example.pinyin: Zhuōzi shàng fàng zhe yí gè xiǎoxiǎo de huāpíng.
example.english: There's a tiny vase sitting on the table.
example.fact: A nanometer is one billionth of a meter — small enough that roughly ten hydrogen atoms lined up in a row would span the distance. Modern computer chips etch transistor features only a few nanometers wide, meaning billions of them fit onto a chip smaller than a fingernail. At that scale, quantum effects like electron tunneling start to matter, one of the main engineering challenges in shrinking chips further.

examples.hanzi: 小狗有一条小小的尾巴。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎogǒu yǒu yì tiáo xiǎoxiǎo de wěiba.
examples.english: The puppy has a tiny tail.

examples.hanzi: 她住在一个小小的村子里。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhù zài yí ge xiǎoxiǎo de cūnzi lǐ.
examples.english: She lives in a tiny village.

components.note: 木 (wood) — trees; 杜 first named a pear tree, as in 树 tree, 林 forest.
土 (tǔ) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 肚 dù.

example.hanzi: 我们要杜绝浪费。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen yào dùjué làngfèi.
example.english: We must put an end to waste.
example.fact: 杜 as a verb sits mostly in 杜绝 ('to eliminate'); it is also a surname, famous for the poet 杜甫. The original sense, a pear-like tree, is rare now.

examples.hanzi: 杜甫是唐朝的大诗人。
examples.pinyin: Dù Fǔ shì Tángcháo de dà shīrén.
examples.english: Du Fu was a great poet of the Tang dynasty.

examples.hanzi: 杜老师是我们的班主任。
examples.pinyin: Dù lǎoshī shì wǒmen de bānzhǔrèn.
examples.english: Teacher Du is our homeroom teacher.

components.note: 衣 (clothes) — a picture of a coat with a collar and sleeves. As a radical it is 衤 on the left: 裤 trousers, 衬 shirt, 被 quilt.

example.hanzi: 他穿着一件白衣。
example.pinyin: Tā chuānzhe yí jiàn báiyī.
example.english: He is wearing a white garment.
example.fact: 衣 is the base of 衣服 (clothes) and 上衣 (top), and as a left-hand radical appears as 衤. The measure word for clothes is 件.

examples.hanzi: 我要把雨衣带上。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yào bǎ yǔyī dàishàng.
examples.english: I'll bring my raincoat.

examples.hanzi: 她把衣服洗干净了。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ yīfu xǐ gānjìng le.
examples.english: She washed the clothes clean.

components.note: 女 (woman) — 女 marks women, as in 妈, 姐; 妇 is a married woman.
彐 (hand) — 彐 is a hand holding a broom (the traditional 婦 had 帚), so a married woman who keeps house.
女 (woman) — a person kneeling with arms crossed; as a radical it heads many female and family words: 妈, 好, 姐.

example.hanzi: 三月八日是国际妇女节。
example.pinyin: Sānyuè bā rì shì Guójì Fùnǚ Jié.
example.english: March 8th is International Women's Day.
example.fact: International Women's Day traces back to 1909, when the Socialist Party of America organized a National Woman's Day in New York to honor a garment workers' strike. The date was fixed at March 8th in 1917 after women textile workers in Petrograd, Russia, staged a strike and protest often credited with helping spark the February Revolution that eventually led to the Tsar's abdication.

examples.hanzi: 那位妇女正在菜市场买菜。
examples.pinyin: Nà wèi fùnǚ zhèngzài càishìchǎng mǎi cài.
examples.english: That woman is buying groceries at the market.

examples.hanzi: 妇女和儿童可以先上车。
examples.pinyin: Fùnǚ hé értóng kěyǐ xiān shàng chē.
examples.english: Women and children may board first.

components.note: 来 (come) — it began as a picture of a wheat plant; the sound was borrowed for "come". 麦 (wheat) still shows it, with a root 夂 added.
氵 (water) — marks water and rivers, as in 河, 海; 源 is the spring where water starts.
原 (yuán) gives the sound exactly: 源 yuán, also in 愿 yuàn.

example.hanzi: 记者一直没有透露这条消息的来源。
example.pinyin: Jìzhě yìzhí méiyǒu tòulù zhè tiáo xiāoxi de láiyuán.
example.english: The reporter never revealed the source of this information.
example.fact: Deep Throat, the anonymous source behind the Watergate scandal reporting by Bob Woodward and Carl Bernstein, kept his identity secret for over 30 years until former FBI associate director Mark Felt revealed himself in 2005. Protecting a source's identity is considered so important in journalism that some reporters have gone to jail rather than reveal one, a principle tested in cases like that of New York Times reporter Judith Miller in 2005.

examples.hanzi: 这个消息的来源可靠吗？
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiāoxi de láiyuán kěkào ma?
examples.english: Is the source of this news reliable?

examples.hanzi: 这种水果的来源是南方。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng shuǐguǒ de láiyuán shì nánfāng.
examples.english: This kind of fruit originates in the south.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — 刂 is 刀 (knife) as in 到, 别, 利; 判 is to cut in half, so to separate and decide.
半 (bàn) — near sound — 判 is pàn; 半 means half.
冫 (ice) — here the ice form of 氵 (water): 决 first meant to break a dam, so a decisive break.
夬 (guài) is a loose sound clue for jué; 夬 also sounds out 快 kuài and 块 kuài.

example.hanzi: 法官宣读了对被告的判决。
example.pinyin: Fǎguān xuāndú le duì bèigào de pànjué.
example.english: The judge read out the verdict against the defendant.
example.fact: The right to a trial by jury traces back to Magna Carta in 1215, which limited the English king's power to imprison free men without lawful judgment. The number twelve, still standard for many juries today, has no single confirmed origin, though some historians link it to the twelve tribes of Israel or the twelve apostles as symbolically complete groups.

examples.hanzi: 法院已经作出了判决。
examples.pinyin: Fǎyuàn yǐjīng zuòchū le pànjué.
examples.english: The court has already issued its judgment.

examples.hanzi: 他不满意法院的判决。
examples.pinyin: Tā bù mǎnyì fǎyuàn de pànjué.
examples.english: He is not satisfied with the court's ruling.

components.note: ⻊ (foot, form of 足) — feet and travel: 跑, 跳, 跟; 路 is a road.
各 (gè) is a loose sound clue; same part in 洛 luò, 落 luò, 客 kè.
纟 (thread, simplified 糸) — silk and cord: 红, 给, 组; 线 is thread or line.
戋 (jiān) is a loose sound clue; same part in 浅 qiǎn, 钱 qián and 残 cán.

example.hanzi: 我们改变了去机场的路线，避开了堵车。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen gǎibiàn le qù jīchǎng de lùxiàn, bìkāi le dǔchē.
example.english: We changed our route to the airport to avoid the traffic jam.
example.fact: The GPS satellite network relies on atomic clocks accurate enough that a timing error of just one microsecond would translate into a position error of about 300 meters on the ground. Because satellites orbiting at high speed and altitude experience time slightly differently under Einstein's theories of relativity, GPS systems must correct for both special and general relativistic effects, or reported locations would drift by several kilometers per day.

examples.hanzi: 这条旅游路线要走三天。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo lǚyóu lùxiàn yào zǒu sān tiān.
examples.english: This tourist route takes three days.

examples.hanzi: 请按照这条路线走。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng ànzhào zhè tiáo lùxiàn zǒu.
examples.english: Please follow this route.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — cutting and sharpness: 利, 别, 到; 刻 is to carve, and the carved marks on a clock became quarter hours.
亥 (hài) is only a loose sound hint; same part in 孩 hái and 核 hé.

example.hanzi: 现在是三点一刻。
example.pinyin: Xiànzài shì sān diǎn yí kè.
example.english: It's now a quarter past three.
example.fact: 刻 means 'quarter hour' (一刻 = 15 min), so 三点一刻 is 3:15 and 差一刻 'a quarter to'. The idea of carving also yields 立刻 and 此刻 'at this moment'.

examples.hanzi: 他在木头上刻了一朵花。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài mùtou shang kè le yì duǒ huā.
examples.english: He carved a flower on the wood.

examples.hanzi: 这一刻我很感动。
examples.pinyin: Zhè yí kè wǒ hěn gǎndòng.
examples.english: At this moment I'm very moved.

components.note: 土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 场 field, 城 city, 坐 sit.
也 (yě) is a loose sound clue for dì; 也 also sounds out 他 tā and 池 chí.
毛 (fur) — marks hair and wool, as in 羽, 毯 itself; 毯 is a woollen rug.
炎 (yán) is a loose hint for tǎn; 谈 tán and 淡 dàn share it.

example.hanzi: 客厅里铺着一块红色的地毯。
example.pinyin: Kètīng lǐ pù zhe yí kuài hóngsè de dìtǎn.
example.english: A red carpet is laid out in the living room.
example.fact: The Pazyryk Carpet, discovered frozen in a Siberian burial mound in 1949, is the oldest known pile carpet in the world, dated to roughly the 5th century BC. Remarkably well preserved by the permafrost, its intricate wool knots — over 3,600 per square inch — show that sophisticated carpet-weaving techniques existed more than two thousand years ago.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们坐在地毯上玩积木。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen zuò zài dìtǎn shàng wán jīmù.
examples.english: The children are sitting on the carpet playing with blocks.

examples.hanzi: 这块地毯需要洗一洗。
examples.pinyin: Zhè kuài dìtǎn xūyào xǐ yi xǐ.
examples.english: This rug needs to be washed.

components.note: 亻 (person) — person radical — 依 is to lean on someone.
衣 (yī) — same sound — 依 is yī, like 衣.
告 (gào) — loose hint — 靠 is kào; 告 also sounds out 造 zào and 酷 kù.
非 (not) — two wings pointing away from each other, so back to back; as a memory aid, 靠 is leaning your back on something.

example.hanzi: 沙漠里的绿洲居民依靠地下水生存。
example.pinyin: Shāmò lǐ de lǜzhōu jūmín yīkào dìxiàshuǐ shēngcún.
example.english: Oasis residents in the desert rely on groundwater to survive.
example.fact: Many desert oases are fed by ancient 'fossil water' aquifers, groundwater deposited thousands to millions of years ago during wetter climate periods and not meaningfully replenished today. Libya's Great Man-Made River project taps such fossil aquifers beneath the Sahara, piping billions of liters of ancient water to coastal cities — a resource that, once drawn down, may take millennia to naturally refill.

examples.hanzi: 孩子不能总是依靠父母。
examples.pinyin: Háizi bù néng zǒngshì yīkào fùmǔ.
examples.english: Children can't always rely on their parents.

examples.hanzi: 我们要依靠自己的努力。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào yīkào zìjǐ de nǔlì.
examples.english: We have to rely on our own efforts.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 拉, 提; 扔 is to throw.
乃 (nǎi) is only a loose sound hint for rēng.
扌 (hand) — hand radical for actions — 掉 is to drop or lose hold.

example.hanzi: 他把过期的食物都扔掉了。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ guòqī de shíwù dōu rēngdiào le.
example.english: He threw away all the expired food.
example.fact: Food waste buried in landfills decomposes without enough oxygen, producing methane, a greenhouse gas more than 25 times more potent than carbon dioxide over a 100-year period. The United Nations estimates roughly a third of all food produced worldwide is lost or wasted, which is why some cities now mandate separate composting of food scraps to divert them from landfills.

examples.hanzi: 别把还能用的东西扔掉。
examples.pinyin: Bié bǎ hái néng yòng de dōngxi rēngdiào.
examples.english: Don't throw away things that are still usable.

examples.hanzi: 我把旧衣服都扔掉了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ jiù yīfu dōu rēngdiào le.
examples.english: I threw away all the old clothes.

components.note: 衤 (clothing) — marks clothes, as in 衬, 衫, 裤; 裸 is to be unclothed.
果 (guǒ) hints at the sound: 裸 luǒ is close, as in 课 kè and 颗 kē.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: 体 is a person's body.
本 (root) — the root of a person, the body; the traditional form was 體 with 骨 (bone).

example.hanzi: 那座雕像描绘的是一个裸体的战士。
example.pinyin: Nà zuò diāoxiàng miáohuì de shì yí gè luǒtǐ de zhànshì.
example.english: That statue depicts a nude warrior.
example.fact: Ancient Greek sculptors idealized the nude male form in statues like the Discobolus, believing physical perfection reflected moral and civic virtue, a tradition later revived during the Renaissance. Michelangelo's David, carved between 1501 and 1504 from a single block of marble previously abandoned by two other sculptors as flawed, stands over 5 meters tall and remains one of the most famous nude sculptures in history.

examples.hanzi: 海滩上不允许裸体。
examples.pinyin: Hǎitān shàng bù yǔnxǔ luǒtǐ.
examples.english: Nudity is not allowed on the beach.

examples.hanzi: 美术课上，学生们画了一幅裸体素描。
examples.pinyin: Měishù kè shàng, xuéshengmen huà le yì fú luǒtǐ sùmiáo.
examples.english: In art class, the students drew a nude sketch.

components.note: 阝 (mound, hill) — left-side 阝 is 阜 (mound), as in 阳, 院; 陷 is falling into a pit.
臽 (xiàn) — same sound — 陷 is xiàn; 臽 also sounds out 馅 xiàn.
阝 (hill, from 阜) — marks mounds and the ground, as in 院, 阶, 防; 阱 is a pit dug in the earth.
井 (jǐng) gives the sound exactly: 阱 jǐng, and 井 is a well, itself a pit.

example.hanzi: 猎人在森林里设了一个陷阱。
example.pinyin: Lièrén zài sēnlín lǐ shè le yí gè xiànjǐng.
example.english: The hunter set a trap in the forest.
example.fact: Pitcher plants lure insects with sweet nectar into a slippery, tube-shaped trap lined with downward-pointing hairs that make climbing back out nearly impossible. Once inside, the insect drowns in a pool of digestive fluid at the bottom, which the plant uses to extract nitrogen and other nutrients scarce in the boggy soils where these plants typically grow.

examples.hanzi: 这是一个陷阱，不要上当。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yí ge xiànjǐng, búyào shàngdàng.
examples.english: This is a trap; don't fall for it.

examples.hanzi: 他们掉进了对手设下的陷阱。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen diào jìn le duìshǒu shèxià de xiànjǐng.
examples.english: They fell into the trap their opponent set.

components.note: 公 (public) — 八 over 厶: dividing 八 what is private 厶; so "shared, public, fair".
止 (foot) — a foot heading straight for a target line: upright, correct. 正 gives sound to 证 zhèng, 整 zhěng and 政 zhèng.

example.hanzi: 大家都希望法律能对每个人公正。
example.pinyin: Dàjiā dōu xīwàng fǎlǜ néng duì měi gè rén gōngzhèng.
example.english: Everyone hopes the law can be fair to everyone.
example.fact: The blindfolded figure of Lady Justice, holding a scale and sword, traces back to the Roman goddess Justitia and, further, to the Egyptian goddess Ma'at, said to weigh the hearts of the dead against a feather to judge their worthiness. The blindfold, a later addition dating to around the 16th century, was meant to symbolize impartiality — that justice should not be swayed by who stands before it.

examples.hanzi: 老师对每个学生都很公正。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī duì měi ge xuésheng dōu hěn gōngzhèng.
examples.english: The teacher is very fair to every student.

examples.hanzi: 裁判的判断不够公正。
examples.pinyin: Cáipàn de pànduàn bú gòu gōngzhèng.
examples.english: The referee's decision was not fair enough.

components.note: 心 (heart) — mind and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感: 总 is simplified from 總, whose threads gathered everything together.
⺮ (bamboo) — bamboo, as in 笔 pen, 等 wait, 第: counting rods were once bamboo.
具 (jù, tool) — here the lower part shows hands holding the counting tools.

example.hanzi: 经过三年的努力，他总算通过了考试。
example.pinyin: Jīngguò sān nián de nǔlì, tā zǒngsuàn tōngguò le kǎoshì.
example.english: After three years of effort, he finally passed the exam.
example.fact: Thomas Edison and his team reportedly tested thousands of filament materials before settling on carbonized bamboo for a commercially practical incandescent light bulb in the late 1870s. Edison later described earlier failures not as failures but as having 'found 10,000 ways that won't work,' a mindset historians credit with driving the systematic, trial-and-error approach of his Menlo Park laboratory.

examples.hanzi: 等了一个小时，公交车总算来了。
examples.pinyin: Děng le yí ge xiǎoshí, gōngjiāochē zǒngsuàn lái le.
examples.english: After waiting an hour, the bus finally came.

examples.hanzi: 雨总算停了，我们可以出去玩了。
examples.pinyin: Yǔ zǒngsuàn tíng le, wǒmen kěyǐ chūqù wán le.
examples.english: The rain has finally stopped, so we can go out to play.

components.note: 真 (zhēn) is a sound clue for 镇 zhèn and 慎 shèn; 真 means real, true.
心 (heart) — a picture of a heart. Written 忄 on the left (快, 怕) and 心 at the bottom (想, 思, 忘); it marks feelings and thoughts.

example.hanzi: 他真心希望朋友们都能过得幸福。
example.pinyin: Tā zhēnxīn xīwàng péngyǒumen dōu néng guò de xìngfú.
example.english: He sincerely hopes his friends can all live happily.
example.fact: The handshake is believed to have originated as a gesture of peace in ancient times, showing neither party was carrying a hidden weapon in their right hand. Some historians trace depictions of clasped hands, called 'dexiosis,' back to 5th-century BC Greek funerary art, where it symbolized trust and farewell between the living and the dead.

examples.hanzi: 我真心感谢你的帮助。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhēnxīn gǎnxiè nǐ de bāngzhù.
examples.english: I sincerely thank you for your help.

examples.hanzi: 她对朋友一向很真心。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì péngyou yíxiàng hěn zhēnxīn.
examples.english: She has always been sincere with her friends.

meanings: auxiliary showing sth happened in the past

components.note: 来 (come) — it began as a picture of a wheat plant; the sound was borrowed for "come". 麦 (wheat) still shows it, with a root 夂 added.
著 (zhù / zhe) — older form of 着: 艹 plant + 者 (zhě) as sound. 着 is a variant with 羊 over 目; neither part gives the 'in progress' sense.
目 (eye) — the bottom. The eye family: 看, 眼, 睛, 睡. In 着 it is only part of a variant shape. Memory aid: 睡着 — eyes 目 shut, asleep.

example.hanzi: 你刚才说什么来着？
example.pinyin: Nǐ gāngcái shuō shénme láizhe?
example.english: What did you just say again?
example.fact: The 'tip-of-the-tongue' phenomenon, when you're sure you know a word but can't quite retrieve it, has been studied since psychologists Roger Brown and David McNeill formally named it in a 1966 paper. Brain imaging studies suggest the sought-for word is often stored correctly in memory the whole time — the trouble lies in a temporary failure to link its sound to its meaning during retrieval, not in forgetting the word itself.

examples.hanzi: 你昨天去哪儿来着？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zuótiān qù nǎr láizhe?
examples.english: Where did you go yesterday, again?

examples.hanzi: 他叫什么名字来着？我忘了。
examples.pinyin: Tā jiào shénme míngzi láizhe? Wǒ wàng le.
examples.english: What was his name again? I forgot.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — words passed down through ten 十 generations of mouths — old; 古 also sounds out 姑 gū and 故 gù.
耂 (old) — 老 pictures an old person with long hair leaning on a staff; the short form 耂 is also in 考 test and 孝 filial.

example.hanzi: 这座古老的城墙已经有两千年的历史了。
example.pinyin: Zhè zuò gǔlǎo de chéngqiáng yǐjīng yǒu liǎngqiān nián de lìshǐ le.
example.english: This ancient city wall already has a two-thousand-year history.
example.fact: Contrary to a popular myth, the Great Wall of China is not visible to the naked eye from the Moon — it is only a few meters wide, far too narrow to be seen from such a distance despite its roughly 21,000-kilometer total length across multiple dynasties. Astronauts in low Earth orbit, a few hundred kilometers up, have reported it is difficult to spot even from there without magnification, especially compared to highways or airports.

examples.hanzi: 这座古老的寺庙吸引了很多游客。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò gǔlǎo de sìmiào xīyǐn le hěn duō yóukè.
examples.english: This ancient temple attracts a lot of tourists.

examples.hanzi: 爷爷给我讲了一个古老的故事。
examples.pinyin: Yéye gěi wǒ jiǎng le yí ge gǔlǎo de gùshi.
examples.english: Grandpa told me an ancient story.

meanings: (of a turn of events) not too encouraging

components.note: 一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
女 (woman) — 女 marks women, as in 妈, 姐; 妙 first meant fine and delicate.
少 (shǎo) — loose hint — 妙 is miào; 少 also means few or little.

example.hanzi: 天空突然变黑，情况看起来不妙。
example.pinyin: Tiānkōng tūrán biàn hēi, qíngkuàng kàn qǐlái bùmiào.
example.english: The sky suddenly turned black — the situation looked ominous.
example.fact: A greenish tint to the sky before a storm is often associated with hail-producing supercell thunderstorms, caused by sunlight scattering through the storm's massive, deep cloud layers combined with large water droplets and ice. Meteorologists still debate the exact mechanism, but the color has long served as a folk warning sign for approaching severe weather, including tornadoes.

examples.hanzi: 糟糕，情况不妙，我们快走。
examples.pinyin: Zāogāo, qíngkuàng búmiào, wǒmen kuài zǒu.
examples.english: Oh no, things look bad; let's go quickly.

examples.hanzi: 他脸色不妙，是不是病了？
examples.pinyin: Tā liǎnsè búmiào, shì bu shì bìng le?
examples.english: He looks unwell; is he sick?

components.note: 亻 (person) — marks people and their actions, as in 你, 做; 伪 is a person acting a part: fake.
为 (wéi) hints at the sound: 伪 wěi is close.
衣 (clothing) — clothes and wear: 衬, 被, 袋; 装 is dress, then to pretend or to load.
壮 (zhuàng) is a near sound match for zhuāng; also in 状 zhuàng and 妆 zhuāng.

example.hanzi: 士兵们用树叶把自己伪装起来。
example.pinyin: Shìbīngmen yòng shùyè bǎ zìjǐ wěizhuāng qǐlái.
example.english: The soldiers camouflaged themselves with leaves.
example.fact: Cuttlefish can change the color and texture of their skin within a fraction of a second using thousands of pigment-filled cells called chromatophores, controlled directly by their nervous system. Remarkably, cuttlefish are colorblind, yet they can still match complex background patterns almost perfectly — a puzzle that has led researchers to suspect they may sense light through photoreceptors in their skin as well as their eyes.

examples.hanzi: 小虫子会伪装成树叶。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎo chóngzi huì wěizhuāng chéng shùyè.
examples.english: Small insects disguise themselves as leaves.

examples.hanzi: 他伪装成客人混进了酒店。
examples.pinyin: Tā wěizhuāng chéng kèrén hùn jìn le jiǔdiàn.
examples.english: He disguised himself as a guest and slipped into the hotel.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — a house, as in 家, 安, 室; 宴 is a feast at home.
妟 (yàn) gives the sound exactly: 宴 yàn.
会 (meet, can) — simplified from 會, a lid on a container: bringing things together; hence meeting, then "can" (huì).

example.hanzi: 公司为退休的员工举办了一场宴会。
example.pinyin: Gōngsī wèi tuìxiū de yuángōng jǔbàn le yì chǎng yànhuì.
example.english: The company held a banquet for the retiring employee.
example.fact: Ancient Roman banquets, especially among the elite, could last many hours and feature exotic dishes such as roasted flamingo or stuffed dormice, eaten while reclining on couches rather than sitting at a table. Some wealthy hosts employed a designated slave called a 'nomenclator' whose sole job was to remember and announce the names of arriving guests, a kind of living guest list.

examples.hanzi: 今晚的宴会在六点开始。
examples.pinyin: Jīnwǎn de yànhuì zài liù diǎn kāishǐ.
examples.english: Tonight's banquet starts at six.

examples.hanzi: 我们受邀参加了他们的婚礼宴会。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen shòuyāo cānjiā le tāmen de hūnlǐ yànhuì.
examples.english: We were invited to their wedding banquet.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — the top part, as in 和 and 秋. Memory aid: a woman (女) bending under a bundle of grain; grain plus woman gives 'bend / entrust', now 'appoint'.
女 (woman) — the bottom part and radical, as in 她 she and 妈 mom. Here it hints at a yielding, bending figure rather than a woman.
扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: 托 is to hold up with the hand.
乇 (tuō) gives the exact sound.

example.hanzi: 他委托律师处理这起案件。
example.pinyin: Tā wěituō lǜshī chǔlǐ zhè qǐ ànjiàn.
example.english: He entrusted the lawyer to handle this case.
example.fact: The modern escrow system, where a neutral third party holds funds or documents until conditions of an agreement are met, has roots in medieval English law, where the word 'scroll' (from Old French 'escroue') referred to a written deed held in trust by someone other than the two contracting parties. Real estate transactions worldwide still rely on the same basic idea: a trusted intermediary who releases assets only once agreed conditions are satisfied.

examples.hanzi: 我委托朋友帮我取包裹。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ wěituō péngyou bāng wǒ qǔ bāoguǒ.
examples.english: I asked a friend to pick up my parcel for me.

examples.hanzi: 这件事已经委托给专业公司了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì yǐjīng wěituō gěi zhuānyè gōngsī le.
examples.english: This matter has already been entrusted to a professional company.

components.note: 白 (white, bright) — gives sound to 拍 pāi, 怕 pà, 伯 bó and 泊 bó. Meaning: white, clear, plain, hence "明白" understand.
宀 (roof) — a house or building, as in 家, 安, 室; 宫 is a palace, a grand house.

example.hanzi: 总统在白宫接见了外国代表团。
example.pinyin: Zǒngtǒng zài Báigōng jiējiàn le wàiguó dàibiǎotuán.
example.english: The president received the foreign delegation at the White House.
example.fact: The White House was originally built with sandstone that was whitewashed to protect it from the elements, one popular explanation for its name, though the name wasn't made official until Theodore Roosevelt did so in 1901. British troops burned the building in 1814 during the War of 1812, and much of the outer stone walls seen today are the same scorched sandstone that survived and was later restored.

examples.hanzi: 很多游客来白宫参观。
examples.pinyin: Hěn duō yóukè lái Báigōng cānguān.
examples.english: Many tourists come to visit the White House.

examples.hanzi: 新闻里说白宫发表了声明。
examples.pinyin: Xīnwén lǐ shuō Báigōng fābiǎo le shēngmíng.
examples.english: The news says the White House issued a statement.

meanings: to issue (an official document or credential)

components.note: 发 (send out, hair) — two characters merged in simplified writing: 發 fā "emit, issue" and 髮 fà "hair" (头发).
辶 (movement, road) — 辶 marks going and moving, as in 过, 进, 迷; 送 is walking someone off, or delivering.

example.hanzi: 请把这份文件发送到我的邮箱。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ zhè fèn wénjiàn fāsòng dào wǒ de yóuxiāng.
example.english: Please send this document to my email.
example.fact: The first email was sent in 1971 by computer engineer Ray Tomlinson, who also chose the @ symbol to separate the username from the host computer's name — a convention still used in virtually every email address today. Tomlinson later said he didn't remember the exact content of that first test message and considered the choice of the @ symbol more significant than the message itself.

examples.hanzi: 我已经把邮件发送给你了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǐjīng bǎ yóujiàn fāsòng gěi nǐ le.
examples.english: I've already sent the email to you.

examples.hanzi: 信息发送失败，请再试一次。
examples.pinyin: Xìnxī fāsòng shībài, qǐng zài shì yí cì.
examples.english: The message failed to send; please try again.

components.note: 冫 (water, ice) — 冲 is the simplified 沖: a water element (冫) beside 中, so water rushing; this form is a water cousin of 冰 and 冷.
中 (zhōng) — near sound — 冲 is chōng; 中 also sounds out 钟 zhōng.
穴 (cave, hole) — the radical of holes and hollow spaces, as in 空 empty, 窗 window, 穿 pierce.
犬 (dog) — a dog bursting out of its den 穴: the picture of something sudden and unexpected.

example.hanzi: 两国因边境问题发生了冲突。
example.pinyin: Liǎng guó yīn biānjìng wèntí fāshēng le chōngtū.
example.english: The two countries had a conflict over the border issue.
example.fact: The Åland Islands dispute between Sweden and Finland in the early 1920s is often cited as one of the first conflicts resolved through the newly formed League of Nations, which granted the islands to Finland while guaranteeing strong autonomy and demilitarization. The arrangement has held peacefully for over a century and is frequently studied as a model for resolving territorial disputes without war.

examples.hanzi: 两个孩子因为玩具起了冲突。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng ge háizi yīnwèi wánjù qǐ le chōngtū.
examples.english: The two children had a conflict over a toy.

examples.hanzi: 这次会议和我的课时间冲突了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì huìyì hé wǒ de kè shíjiān chōngtū le.
examples.english: This meeting conflicts with my class time.

components.note: 犬 (dog) — a picture of a dog. As 犭 it marks animals, as in 狗 dog, 猫 cat, 狼 wolf.

example.hanzi: 警犬找到了失踪的孩子。
example.pinyin: Jǐngquǎn zhǎodào le shīzōng de háizi.
example.english: The police dog found the missing child.
example.fact: 犬 is the literary or technical word for dog, while 狗 is the spoken one. It appears in 警犬, 导盲犬 (guide dog), 宠物犬 and 犬齿 (canine tooth).

examples.hanzi: 这只牧羊犬很聪明。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhī mùyángquǎn hěn cōngming.
examples.english: This sheepdog is very smart.

examples.hanzi: 他在公园里遇到了一只流浪犬。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài gōngyuán li yùdào le yì zhī liúlàngquǎn.
examples.english: He met a stray dog in the park.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; 指 is the finger or to point.
旨 (zhǐ) sounds exactly like 指; also in 脂 zhī.
示 (show) — an altar, a table for offerings; as the radical 礻 it marks rites and spirits: 神, 礼, 福, 社, 祝.

example.hanzi: 老板给员工下达了新的指示。
example.pinyin: Lǎobǎn gěi yuángōng xiàdá le xīn de zhǐshì.
example.english: The boss issued new instructions to the employees.
example.fact: After a prototype of the Boeing B-17 crashed in 1935 due to pilot error despite the crew's extensive experience, the U.S. Army Air Corps developed the first standardized pilot checklist rather than relying purely on training and memory. That simple written instruction list is credited with helping make the B-17 one of the most reliable aircraft of World War II, and checklists remain a cornerstone of aviation safety today.

examples.hanzi: 医生给了我一些饮食指示。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng gěi le wǒ yìxiē yǐnshí zhǐshì.
examples.english: The doctor gave me some dietary instructions.

examples.hanzi: 箭头指示出口在右边。
examples.pinyin: Jiàntóu zhǐshì chūkǒu zài yòubiān.
examples.english: The arrow indicates that the exit is on the right.

meanings: to have no other option but to ...

components.note: 只 (only; measure word) — two old characters merged: 隻 zhī "a single (bird), measure word" and 只 zhǐ "only".
女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 姐.
子 (child) — a woman with her child: the picture of something good.

example.hanzi: 因为下大雨，我们只好取消了野餐。
example.pinyin: Yīnwèi xià dàyǔ, wǒmen zhǐhǎo qǔxiāo le yěcān.
example.english: Because of the heavy rain, we had no choice but to cancel the picnic.
example.fact: Modern weather radar can detect rain up to about 250 kilometers away by bouncing microwave pulses off water droplets and measuring how the signal returns, a technique developed from radar systems built during World War II. Operators noticed that rain and snow created unwanted 'clutter' on military radar screens meant to detect aircraft, and that same clutter became the basis of the meteorological radar used for forecasts today.

examples.hanzi: 手机没电了，我只好走路回家。
examples.pinyin: Shǒujī méi diàn le, wǒ zhǐhǎo zǒulù huí jiā.
examples.english: My phone ran out of battery, so I had to walk home.

examples.hanzi: 他不在家，我只好改天再来。
examples.pinyin: Tā bú zài jiā, wǒ zhǐhǎo gǎitiān zài lái.
examples.english: He isn't home, so I'll have to come again another day.

components.note: 攵 (tap, strike) — marks actions, as in 教, 改, 放; 散 is to scatter (sàn) or to be loose (sǎn).
止 (foot) — two footprints, one above the other, make a step; the same 止 is in 走 walk and 跑 run.

example.hanzi: 晚饭后，他喜欢去公园散步。
example.pinyin: Wǎnfàn hòu, tā xǐhuān qù gōngyuán sànbù.
example.english: After dinner, he likes to take a walk in the park.
example.fact: Studies on walking speed and health have found that a brisk pace of roughly 100 steps per minute is associated with measurable cardiovascular benefits, sometimes described informally as a 'cadence-based' threshold for moderate exercise. Other research has linked as few as a couple thousand extra daily steps to a meaningfully lower risk of cardiovascular disease, even without any other change in exercise habits.

examples.hanzi: 我每天早上都去河边散步。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān zǎoshang dōu qù hébiān sànbù.
examples.english: I go for a walk by the river every morning.

examples.hanzi: 我们一边散步，一边聊天。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yìbiān sànbù, yìbiān liáotiān.
examples.english: We chatted while taking a walk.

components.note: 化 (change) — one person 亻 beside an upside-down person 匕 — a change of state; 化 is to change, as in 文化 and 变化.
女 (woman) — marks women, as in 妈, 姐, 好; 妆 is make-up.
丬 (a form of 爿) hints at the sound: 妆 zhuāng, close to 壮 zhuàng, 状 zhuàng and 装 zhuāng.

example.hanzi: 她每天早上都要花半小时化妆。
example.pinyin: Tā měitiān zǎoshang dōu yào huā bàn xiǎoshí huàzhuāng.
example.english: She spends half an hour putting on makeup every morning.
example.fact: Ancient Egyptians of both sexes commonly wore kohl eyeliner as early as 4000 BC, partly for its believed ability to protect eyes from the sun's glare and ward off infection, in addition to its cosmetic effect. Chemical analysis of ancient Egyptian cosmetic containers has found lead-based compounds that, in small amounts, may have boosted the skin's production of nitric oxide, offering a genuine, if unintended, antibacterial benefit.

examples.hanzi: 她出门前总要化妆。
examples.pinyin: Tā chūmén qián zǒngyào huàzhuāng.
examples.english: She always puts on makeup before going out.

examples.hanzi: 演员在后台化妆。
examples.pinyin: Yǎnyuán zài hòutái huàzhuāng.
examples.english: The actor is putting on makeup backstage.

components.note: 木 (wood) — a wooden cabinet; also in 桌 table, 椅 chair.
巨 (jù) is only a stand-in; the traditional 櫃 used 贵 guì for the sound.

example.hanzi: 衣服都在衣柜里。
example.pinyin: Yīfu dōu zài yīguì lǐ.
example.english: The clothes are all in the wardrobe.
example.fact: 柜 in 柜子 means a cupboard or cabinet, and in 衣柜 (wardrobe) or 书柜 (bookcase). 柜台 is a shop 'counter', so 去柜台付款 means 'pay at the counter'.

examples.hanzi: 请把书放进书柜里。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ shū fàng jìn shūguì li.
examples.english: Please put the books into the bookcase.

examples.hanzi: 请到前面的柜台付款。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng dào qiánmiàn de guìtái fùkuǎn.
examples.english: Please pay at the counter up front.
